idiom_name: JSP scriptlets and expressions in a .jsp page (Jakarta Server Pages)
implementation_notes: Jakarta Server Pages is the archetype of this pattern: <% ... %> is a scriptlet executed in the page's service method, <%= ... %> writes an expression to the JspWriter, <%@ page %> sets response properties and imports, and the container compiles the page once and caches the generated servlet, so the page owns request handling end to end (JSP Model 1). Model access happens through whatever the script can reach - request attributes, a DAO, a service locator - and escaping is not automatic, so <%= %> output needs an explicit escape call. Modern practice replaces scriptlets with the expression language, JSTL/custom tags and a controller (Template View plus View Helper); scriptlets remain justified only for genuinely small, short-lived pages that a bean helper keeps readable.
code_sketch:
<%@ page contentType="text/html; charset=UTF-8" %> <%@ page import="com.acme.UserRepository, java.util.List" %> <% List users = UserRepository.get().findActive(); %>
    <% for (User u : users) { %>
  • <%= escapeHtml(u.getName()) %> (<%= u.getLogins() %>)
    • <% } %>
pitfalls: <%= expression %> writes raw output - JSP does not escape it - so every interpolated value needs an explicit escape call, while the expression language and JSTL tag output are the safer paths.

Scriptlet code runs inside the generated servlet's per-request method, but declarations (<%! %>) become instance fields shared across requests: caching page state there is the classic JSP thread-safety bug.
Pages are compiled by the container on first request, so a typo becomes a runtime error page rather than a build failure, and each page carries its own compiled class and cache entry.

Reading session attributes, JDBC connections or thread-locals inside the script couples the page to container state, making it impossible to render outside the container and hard to reuse from another entry point.
